meta.title: Automation ROI Ranker
meta.note: A transparent estimator, not a guarantee. The automatable and oversight factors are practitioner heuristics shown on screen so you can sanity-check and adjust the inputs.

sensitivities.name: Low
sensitivities.note: A wrong result is cheap and easy to catch, so it can run unattended.

sensitivities.name: Medium
sensitivities.note: Mostly automatable, with spot checks or an exception queue.

sensitivities.name: High
sensitivities.note: A wrong result is costly, so keep a human in the loop on the decision.

patterns.name: SOAR playbook
patterns.blurb: A security orchestration playbook that triggers on an event, gathers context, decides, and acts across your tools.
skeleton: Trigger: the event or alert that starts the playbook
Enrich: pull context from your tools automatically
Decide: apply rules or a risk score to branch
Act: contain, ticket, or notify based on the branch
Record: write the outcome back for audit and metrics

patterns.name: Scheduled script or job
patterns.blurb: A script on a schedule or pipeline trigger that collects, transforms, and delivers, with an alert only when it breaks.
skeleton: Schedule: run on a cron or pipeline trigger
Collect: pull the data or evidence from the source
Transform: normalize it into the format you need
Deliver: file, ticket, dashboard, or storage location
Alert on failure: notify a human only when the job breaks

patterns.name: AI-assisted triage with a human gate
patterns.blurb: A model drafts a summary and suggested disposition; a human approves before anything acts, so judgment stays with a person.
skeleton: Intake: collect the item and its context
Summarize: the model drafts a summary and suggested disposition
Human gate: an analyst approves, edits, or rejects
Act: execute the approved action automatically
Learn: capture corrections to improve the prompts and rules

patterns.name: Compliance-as-code automation
patterns.blurb: Control checks expressed as code or queries that gather evidence on a schedule and flag drift before an audit.
skeleton: Define: express the control check as code or a query
Collect: gather evidence from systems on a schedule
Evaluate: compare current state to the required state
Report: produce pass or fail evidence for auditors
Alert: flag drift so it is fixed before the audit
